rich_summary: This section recounts the origin and rise of Ganapati (Ganesha) and several mythic episodes around Shiva. Parvati fashions a clay guardian, Ganapati, to protect her privacy while bathing. When Shiva returns to Kailasa and is blocked by the boy, he angrily beheads him. Parvati’s grief compels Shiva to restore the child to life by attaching the head of the elephant-demon Gajasura, declaring him his son and granting him primacy in worship as Vighnesvara, remover of obstacles. Ganapati later wins lordship over the divine hosts by wisely circumambulating his parents instead of racing around the world. He is crowned, married to Siddhi and Buddhi, and honored by the gods. The chapter then turns to cosmic conflicts: the destruction of the Tripura demon cities by Shiva and the rise of the formidable demon Jalandhara.

top_scenes.scene_text: Shiva stands before the fallen body of the clay-born guardian while Parvati weeps, as attendants bring the severed elephant head of Gajasura to restore the child to life.
Ganapati sits on darbha grass chanting 'Namah Sivaaya' while reverently circling Shiva and Parvati twenty‑one times as divine light surrounds the family.
Cosmic Tripura battle: Shiva rides a celestial chariot made of Earth with Sun and Moon as wheels, Meru as the bow and Vishnu as the arrow aimed at the three shining demon cities.
